refactor: Apply se-edu Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Parts of the codebase deviate from the se-edu Java coding standard
(basic + intermediate) that this project adopts for all sources.

Deviations such as wildcard imports, unbraced conditionals, missing
header Javadoc, misnamed fields, and overlong lines make violations
harder to spot in review and set a poor baseline for future
contributions.

Let's bring all main and test sources into compliance:

* expand Parser's wildcard imports into explicit imports
* brace single-statement conditionals and put each condition on
  its own line (Task, TaskList)
* add missing header Javadoc to public classes and constructors
  (Echo, Ui, Deadline, Event, Todo, and all exception classes)
* rename SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE instance fields that are not
  constants to camelCase (Ui name/separator, Storage saveFile)
* wrap exception messages beyond the 120-character limit without
  changing their text
* separate logical units by one blank line and remove stray
  contributor comments from sources and tests

User-visible behaviour is unchanged: error strings stay identical,
./gradlew test passes, and all 10 console UI test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Mandate se-edu Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
AI assistants working in this repo had no project-level rule pointing
them at the adopted se-edu Java coding standard, so generated or
reviewed code could drift from it again.

Let's add a project-specific requirement that mandates invoking the
$seedu-java-coding-standard skill for all Java code and fixing
violations on contact.

The skill itself lives under the gitignored .opencode/.codex skill
directories, so AGENTS.md carries the enforceable mandate.

Commit messages and branch names in this repo followed no documented
convention, so history quality depended on whoever happened to commit.

Let's extend the Git requirements to mandate the $seedu-git-standard
skill whenever proposing or creating commits, naming branches, or
reviewing history.

Like its sibling skill, it lives under the gitignored .opencode/.codex
skill directories; AGENTS.md carries the enforceable mandate.
